summary: the relaxation time and the polymer viscosity of a dilute solution of Hookean dumbbells as an Oldroyd-B fluid, in an engine's own units

inputs.name: bead_drag
inputs.meaning: zeta, the drag coefficient of one bead (the gamma of HOOMD-blue's Brownian method for the bead's type)

inputs.name: spring_constant
inputs.meaning: K of the spring force K R, a spring with no rest length (k of a harmonic bond U = k (r - r0)^2 / 2 with r0 = 0)

inputs.name: dumbbells
inputs.meaning: the number of dumbbells, not of beads

outputs.name: relaxation_time
outputs.meaning: lambda = zeta / (4 K), the relaxation time of the dumbbells' upper-convected Maxwell stress

outputs.name: polymer_viscosity
outputs.meaning: eta_p = n kT lambda with n the dumbbells per volume

validity: Hookean springs of unbounded extension, beads with Stokes drag and no hydrodynamic interaction, dumbbells that do not interact (dilute); finite extensibility, excluded volume or hydrodynamic interaction change both constants, and this skill does not say by how much

source.citation: Morozov and Spagnolie (2015), Introduction to Complex Fluids, chapter 1 of Complex Fluids in Biological Systems (read 2026-11-21, https://people.math.wisc.edu/~spagnolie/Papers/Introduction_to_Complex_Fluids.pdf; mat-20261121-morozov-spagnolie-2015-complex-fluids); Hinch and Harlen, Oldroyd B, and not A? (read 2026-11-21, https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hinch/publications/Oldroyd12b.pdf; mat-20261121-hinch-harlen-oldroyd-b)
source.locus: Morozov and Spagnolie, section 4.4.3, after equation (1.109): identifying a relaxation time lambda = zeta/(4K) and a polymer viscosity eta_p = lambda n kB T, the polymer stress satisfies the upper-convected Maxwell equation (1.110); Hinch and Harlen, section 6: the relaxation time tau = 3 pi mu a/(2 kappa), the same with zeta = 6 pi mu a

note: Written for meta_agent/tasks/034, as the reference against which the HOOMD-blue agent's relaxation time and polymer viscosity, read from its stress autocorrelation, are compared. No value of either source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field.
